scientific_status: reviewed synthesis will qualify unsupported assertions

review.summary: The H8 collagen–GAG interaction model relies on rigid gas-phase fragment energy scans lacking explicit stereochemistry, conformational sampling, solvent, and counterions. Crucially, single-axis rotations and arbitrary ETKDG embedded conformers produce unconverged contact energies that shift significantly when rotation counts change. MLIP evaluations cannot simulate bond-forming crosslinking pathways without explicit reactive training data and transition-state validation.

findings.title: Unspecified stereochemistry and single-conformer rigid docking mask physical binding modes
findings.evidence: RDKit ETKDGv3 embeds SMILES strings without explicit stereochemical flags for glycosidic/sugar centers or conformational sampling of flexible side chains.
findings.implication: Calculated interaction energies depend on arbitrary initial embed conformers rather than ensemble-averaged solution state structures.
findings.recommended_check: Generate stereospecifically defined disaccharide and amino-acid conformer ensembles using explicit force-field or metadynamics sampling.

findings.title: Angular orientation grid insufficiency leads to energy instability and rank reordering
findings.evidence: Increasing orientation count from 6 to 24 shifted Lys|DS-0S minimum energy from -1.86 eV (d=2.8 A) to -1.41 eV (d=2.8 A), altering relative rankings across chemical pairs.
findings.implication: Static 1D/1-axis rotation scans fail to locate true interaction minima, rendering relative energy rankings unconverged.
findings.recommended_check: Perform full 3D rigid-body spherical grid minimization or unbiased molecular dynamics in solution.

findings.title: Mapped coordinate axis measures key-atom distance rather than steric intermolecular contact
findings.evidence: Distances are defined along an axis anchored at specific atom map numbers (e.g. ammonium N to sulfate O) rather than minimum atom-atom contact distance.
findings.implication: Calculated minimum distance d_at_min reflects reference atom separation rather than closest van der Waals contact, risking steric overlap or distant fragment tails.
findings.recommended_check: Report interaction energy as a function of minimum atom-atom distance across all atomic pairs.

findings.title: Experimental literature bounds universal claims of glycation-driven proteoglycan detachment
findings.evidence: Reigle et al. 2008 demonstrated that while glycated collagen bound heparin/keratan sulfate weakly, decorin and biglycan binding remained unaffected.
findings.implication: Hypothesis H8 overgeneralizes GAG detachment, as proteoglycan core-protein contacts can preserve binding independently of GAG-chain glycation.
findings.recommended_check: Distinguish full proteoglycan core-protein binding from isolated disaccharide chain contacts in experimentalSPR assays.

findings.title: Foundation MLIPs evaluated at near-equilibrium cannot predict reactive bond-formation barriers
findings.evidence: AIMNet2/ALCHEMI single-point calculations evaluate nonreactive topology energy surfaces and lack reactive transition-state training data.
findings.implication: MLIP energy surfaces cannot be used to infer oxidative crosslinking reaction rates or chemical kinetics without explicit reactive validation.
findings.recommended_check: Separate classical/MLIP nonreactive dynamics from quantum chemical (QM/MM or ReaxFF) transition-state barrier calculations.

review.strongest_surviving_claim: In simplified gas-phase fragment models, converting positively charged Arg to neutral MG-H1 substantially weakens electrostatic and short-range contact energy with isolated sulfated disaccharides relative to native Arg.
review.decisive_next_experiment: Execute a nonreactive pilot using explicit-solvent OpenMM MD (e.g., Amber ff14SB + GLYCAM06) with Na+/Cl- counterions at 0.15 M ionic strength for a collagen triple-helical peptide (e.g., (OGP)_4-GKA-GER-(OGP)_4) bound to a dermatan sulfate hexasaccharide. Measure potential of mean force (PMF) umbrella sampling binding free energies for Lys vs CML and Arg vs MG-H1. For reactive crosslinking pathways, separately validate DFT/QM-MM barrier heights against experimental kinetic rates before running reactive dynamics.
